summary:
Schleswig-Holstein stands under the German national framework, and it has enacted no statute or ordinance of its own specific to trans people. A trans visitor detained in the state is therefore subject to the national rules with no Schleswig-Holstein variation layered on top of them.

On prison placement, Schleswig-Holstein has no provision of its own governing where a trans prisoner is held. Under the Self-Determination Act (SBGG), in force since 1 November 2024, a prisoner's placement tracks the legal gender entry unless state law excludes it. No Schleswig-Holstein exclusion exists, so the SBGG mechanics and the national placement litigation documented in the parent record are the operative rules for a visitor detained here.

A Verfassungsblog analysis of 18 March 2026 raises constitutional doubts about trans-targeted exception clauses in state prison laws. Schleswig-Holstein has not adopted such a clause, so the doubt is presently prospective for the state rather than an applied restriction.

Schleswig-Holstein has previously acted as an initiator on trans-adjacent protection machinery: it was one of five states to table a joint motion in the Bundesrat calling for a ban on conversion therapy, presented in plenary on 12 April 2019.
tangentialFactors:
The conversion-therapy motion Schleswig-Holstein co-tabled was a coordinated initiative with Hesse, Berlin, Bremen and Saarland, first reported as planned by Zeit Online on 10 April 2019 and presented in plenary two days later. Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt and Thuringia supported the motion, and Bavaria indicated potential support with modifications. The Bundestag approved the federal ban on 7 May 2020 with backing from every party except the AfD.

Debate over trans-targeted exception clauses in prison statutes is running at state level across Germany following the July 2026 placement case, in which a person convicted of neo-Nazi incitement whose legal gender had been changed to female under the Self-Determination Act was sent to a men's prison, prompting public outcry over women's-prison safety. Schleswig-Holstein is not among the states with such a provision, and no equivalent Schleswig-Holstein proceeding is sourced here.
localsOnly:
Schleswig-Holstein residents changing their legal gender do so under the national Self-Determination Act, with no state-level procedure, form or waiting rule of their own to complete.

Schleswig-Holstein's own contribution to trans-adjacent protection is its role as a joint sponsor of the 2019 Bundesrat motion for a conversion-therapy ban, tabled alongside Hesse, Berlin, Bremen and Saarland. The resulting prohibition operates nationally, and Schleswig-Holstein's prison administration has no state statute addressing the placement of trans detainees.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Schleswig-Holstein-specific incident of violence against a trans person, no state-level enforcement record on discrimination complaints, and no Schleswig-Holstein prison-service guidance for trans detainees is sourced in this inventory. Whether the state prison administration applies an internal practice on placement, absent a statute, remains unresolved.

The Schleswig-Holstein correctional legislation itself was not reviewed in these sources, so the absence of a trans-specific provision rests on the sourcing reviewed rather than on a full reading of the state's prison act. The practical outcome of SBGG-based placement in Schleswig-Holstein facilities is likewise not documented here.
